CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness, tingling, and pain in left wrist and hand

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a landscaper who reports left wrist and hand pain and numbness that has been ongoing for approximately several months. Symptoms are most noticeable at night, with patient waking up with the hand asleep and needing to shake it out. Numbness involves all fingers but is more pronounced in the thumb and pointer finger, with occasional numbness in the fifth finger. Patient also reports weakness in the left hand and difficulty with fine manipulation, noting that he drops things due to reduced sensation. No problems reported with the right hand. The patient's work involves repetitive heavy labor including raking and digging in landscaping and yard maintenance.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies history of rheumatoid arthritis. Alcohol use: 1-2 beers on Friday and Saturday weekends.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a landscaper performing yard work, maintenance, and upkeep. Work involves heavy repetitive labor including raking and digging.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs clear to auscultation. Grip strength diminished on left compared to right. Sensation to touch intact on right hand but patient reports sensation feels somewhat abnormal on thumb side compared to pointer finger side. Tinel's sign positive bilaterally.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely related to repetitive occupational activities. Treatment plan includes activity modification with delegation of heavy and repetitive work tasks, application of wrist splint, ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours, EMG study to be ordered to evaluate electrical impulses in fingers, and follow-up in office in 2 weeks. At follow-up visit, will assess for need of further diagnostic testing or possible surgical nerve decompression.
